Canonical records and exact original chargesWrite
$$\tau(r,c)=\bigl(\lfloor r/2\rfloor,\lfloor c/2\rfloor\bigr)$$
for the physical tile containing a point, and let  $\mathscr T(T)$  be an original’s set of endpoint tiles. Its charge is
$$q=|M|+
\bigl|\{z\in H:\tau(z)\in\mathscr T(T)\}\bigr|
-2|\mathscr T(T)|.$$
This uses the immutable original  $T,H,M$ . A support’s subsequent consumption by another original does not remove it from the charge calculation.Consider the right-facing chart
$$(r,c)\longmapsto(h-c,b+r)$$
of  $U(h,d,f)$ , where  $h\ge6$  and  $d,f\ge4$  are even. Directly transforming the canonical constructor gives
$$\begin{aligned}
T={}&
\bigl([0,h-1]\times\{b,b+1\}\bigr)\\
&{}\cup\bigl(\{h-1\}\times[b,b+d]\bigr)
\cup\bigl(\{0\}\times[b,b+f]\bigr),
\end{aligned}$$
where intervals denote integer intervals.The complete support set consists of the following six groups:
$$\begin{array}{ll}
\text{Above the strip:}&
(-1,b),(-1,b+2),\ldots,(-1,b+f),\\
\text{Below the strip:}&
(h,b),(h,b+2),\ldots,(h,b+d),\\
\text{Upper inner lateral supports:}&
(1,b+3),(1,b+5),\ldots,(1,b+f-1),\\
\text{Lower inner lateral supports:}&
(h-2,b+3),(h-2,b+5),\ldots,(h-2,b+d-1),\\
\text{Upper beyond-tip support:}&(0,b+f+1),\\
\text{Lower beyond-tip support:}&(h-1,b+d+1).
\end{array}$$
The left-facing record is its image under
$$(r,c)\longmapsto(r,2b+1-c).$$
This reflection preserves physical tiles, including for negative  $b$ . Consequently the charge counts agree in the two directions.Put  $t=(d+f)/2$ . The canonical matching has
$$\frac h2+\left(\frac h2-1\right)+\frac d2+\frac f2
=h-1+t$$
edges. These are the transported original matching edges. Within each original they have disjoint endpoints, and endpoint disjointness between originals ensures that their union remains a matching.The remaining counts are:Bar startMatching edgesEndpoint tilesOriginal supports inside those tilesCharge $b$  even $h-1+t$  $h/2+t$  $t$  $-1$  $b$  odd $h-1+t$  $h-2+t$  $t-2$  $1-h$ Here is the unrestricted counting argument.For even  $b$ , the bar occupies  $h/2$  whole tiles. Each stem adds half its depth in further tiles, giving  $h/2+t$ . There are  $t-2$  inner lateral supports. For the right-facing record, each terminal has an even column and its beyond-tip support has the next odd column, so both lie in the terminal’s tile. This adds two inside supports. Reflection gives the same result for the left-facing record.For odd  $b$ , the bar occupies two tile columns and therefore  $h$  tiles. Each stem adds depth/2 minus one further tiles, giving  $h+t-2$ . The  $t-2$  inner lateral supports remain inside, but each beyond-tip support lies in the next tile outside the footprint. Supports above and below the strip are outside the footprint in both parities.Thus
$$q_{\rm even}
=(h-1+t)+t-2(h/2+t)=-1$$
and
$$q_{\rm odd}
=(h-1+t)+(t-2)-2(h-2+t)=1-h.$$
This verifies the charge table at arbitrary depths, without interpolation from examples.Recommended replacement for the inaccurate sentence:The inner lateral supports contribute  $t-2$  supports inside the endpoint-tile footprint for either bar parity. For even  $b$ , both beyond-tip supports also lie in the terminal tiles, giving  $t$  inside supports; for odd  $b$ , they lie outside the footprint, leaving  $t-2$ . All supports above and below the strip lie outside the footprint.2. The mixed-tile and event classification is exhaustiveLet  $B=b_{\rm odd}$ . I use “interior-row endpoint” to mean an endpoint in rows  $1,\ldots,h-2$ ; every such endpoint belongs to a bar.Adjacent bars form a matchingEvery bar occupies both its columns at every row. Therefore distinct bars have disjoint two-column intervals, and ordered bar starts differ by at least two.Suppose two starts are  $x,x+2$ . The left source must face left: if it faced right, its extreme-row stems would occupy points of the right bar. Similarly, the right source must face right.A source cannot belong to two such adjacent-bar pairs. As the right member of a pair it would have to face right, whereas as the left member of another pair it would have to face left. Thus the adjacent-bar relation is a matching. In particular, if  $p$  counts the odd adjacent-bar pairs,
$$2p\le B.$$
This is a consequence of complete endpoint records and their disjointness; it does not require completeness.All full mixed tiles come from odd adjacent-bar pairsEvery physical tile within the aligned strip contains at least one interior row. In a full tile, both cells on that row must therefore be bar endpoints.If one bar owns both columns, that original owns all four cells, so the tile is not mixed. Otherwise two different bars own the columns. They must be adjacent bars, and their interface lies within a physical tile column precisely when the left start  $x$  is odd.Consequently, for an odd adjacent-bar pair, the full mixed tiles are exactly
$$\left\{
\left(j,\frac{x+1}{2}\right):
0\le j<h/2
\right\}.$$
There are  $h/2$  of them. Different pairs give disjoint tile sets.A column containing only a stem cannot supply the required interior-row endpoint. This excludes the apparent alternative of completing a tile with a bar on one side and a stem on the other.There is no vertical foreign endpoint adjacencyTake two vertically adjacent endpoints in the strip. At least one lies on an interior row, so its owner has a bar in that column. That bar also owns the other point. The two points therefore cannot have different owners.Every event is consequently horizontal.Each odd adjacent-bar pair contributes exactly  $2h$  eventsFor starts  $x,x+2$ , with  $x$  odd, the interface columns are  $x+1,x+2$ . At every row  $r$ , both directed events occur:
$$\bigl(i,(r,x+1),(r,x+2)\bigr),
\qquad
\bigl(j,(r,x+2),(r,x+1)\bigr).$$
The interface is on the backside of both sources. The explicit support lists above show that neither target is an original support of the emitting source.Thus the pair contributes
$$|F_{\rm pair}|=h/2,\qquad |E_{\rm pair}|=2h,$$
and its tile/event contribution is
$$2|F_{\rm pair}|-|E_{\rm pair}|=-h.$$
For  $h=6$ , this is three mixed tiles and twelve labelled events, giving  $-6$ . Counting only six undirected adjacencies would be incorrect.When  $x$  is even, the interface crosses a physical tile-column boundary, so it contributes neither intratile events nor mixed tiles.Every remaining event is a one-way backside-bar eventOn an extreme row, an interior point of a stem has its horizontal neighbours in its own endpoint set. A terminal’s outward neighbour is its own beyond-tip support. Neither can emit a foreign event outward.An event outside the bar-pair case must therefore emit from the backside of a bar on row  $0$  or  $h-1$ . Its foreign target must be a stem terminal: if that target were an interior stem point, the foreign stem would also occupy the emitting bar point, contradicting endpoint disjointness.The reverse direction is excluded because the bar point is the terminal owner’s immutable beyond-tip support.The backside contact is intratile exactly for an odd bar:
$$b\longrightarrow b-1
\quad\text{for a right-facing source},$$
or
$$b+1\longrightarrow b+2
\quad\text{for a left-facing source}.$$
There is at most one such event for each emitting owner and extreme row. An odd bar already in an adjacent-bar pair has its backside occupied by its partner, so it has no remaining event.Writing  $e$  for their number gives the claimed bound
$$0\le e\le 2(B-2p).$$
This accounts for all directed, source-labelled events, including the asymmetry of bar-to-terminal contacts.3. Exact ledger, arbitrary-height inequality, and nonreuseAll transverse charges are negative, so the source contribution is
$$a+(h-1)B.$$
The preceding classification gives the exact set counts
$$|F(Y)|=\frac h2p,\qquad |E(Y)|=2hp+e.$$
Therefore
$$\boxed{\Phi(Y)=a+(h-1)B-hp-e.}$$
For the proposed lower bound,
$$\begin{aligned}
2\left[\Phi(Y)-a-\left(\frac h2-1\right)B\right]
&=h(B-2p)-2e\\
&\ge(h-4)(B-2p)\\
&\ge0.
\end{aligned}$$
Hence, for every common even  $h\ge6$ ,
$$\boxed{\Phi(Y)\ge a+\left(\frac h2-1\right)B.}$$
At  $h=6$ , this specializes to
$$\boxed{\Phi(Y)\ge a+2B\ge a+B=n.}$$
The allocation genuinely avoids reuse:Each paired odd source belongs to exactly one pair.Each pair owns its distinct interface tiles and all its interface events.Every remaining event is assigned to its emitting owner and its extreme-row label.A source serving as the target of an event contributes no second debit: the reverse direction is excluded by its original support.In particular, the argument does not reserve a selected owner’s surplus and then spend that same surplus elsewhere. All debits occur in one exact global ledger.Both coefficients are sharp. An isolated even bar has charge  $-1$ , no mixed tiles and no events, so its inventory is  $1$ . Two adjacent odd bars facing away have disjoint endpoints for arbitrary allowed, independently chosen depths and give
$$\Phi=2(h-1)-h=h-2
=2\left(\frac h2-1\right).$$
These sharpness claims concern the endpoint-disjoint family theorem; they require no completeness assertion.4. The chamber increment and singleton exclusion use the correct old supportsNormalize the upper old bar to row  $0$ . After adding the spanning upward source  $U_W$ , the remaining pocket is
$$P=[2,7]\times[2,W-1].$$
It begins on an even row and column and ends on an odd row and column. It is therefore a union of whole physical tiles. Its immediate boundary is occupied by core endpoints.Every additional connected source meeting  $P$  stays inside  $P$ : a nearest-neighbour endpoint path leaving it would encounter that occupied boundary. Moreover, the endpoint tiles of a pocket source are disjoint from the core’s endpoint tiles. Thus
$$\Phi(O+U_W+Y)-\Phi(O)
=
\bigl[\Phi(O+U_W)-\Phi(O)\bigr]+\Phi(Y).$$
This accounting separation does not erase inherited supports inside the pocket.The spanning upward source has charge  $+1$ , creates six mixed tiles and eight events against the old inventory, giving
$$\Phi(O+U_W)-\Phi(O)=1+2\cdot6-8=5.$$
Therefore the exact chamber relation is
$$\boxed{\Delta_{\rm chamber}=5+\Phi(Y).}$$
All four inherited interior supports are presentThe upper old  $B=U(W,4,4)$  has exactly these supports inside  $P$ :
$$(3,2),\qquad(3,W-1).$$
The spanning upward source, with chart  $(r,c)\mapsto(9-r,c)$ , contributes
$$(6,2),\qquad(6,W-1).$$
The outer source’s inward supports lie in columns  $1,W$ , outside  $P$ , and other old bars contribute no support inside this pocket.Translate by  $(-2,-2)$  and put  $N=W-2$ . The inherited support set inside the normalized pocket is exactly
$$\boxed{
\{(1,0),(1,N-1),(4,0),(4,N-1)\}.
}$$
These are original retained supports, not optional auxiliary constraints.A singleton cannot be completeSuppose  $Y$  consists of one transverse original.Its row- $0$  beyond-tip support is not its own endpoint. If that support lies inside the pocket, it has two occupied endpoint neighbours:its own terminal;the old boundary endpoint directly above it.There is no other pocket source to consume it, and the old core has no endpoint inside the pocket. This contradicts completeness.The beyond-tip support must therefore lie immediately outside a vertical side, forcing the row- $0$  terminal to column  $0$  or  $N-1$ .At that column, the inherited row- $1$  side support has both an old wall neighbour and the new terminal neighbour. It must also be consumed. But the sole source cannot consume it: its interior-row endpoints are only its bar columns, while its terminal lies at least
$$f-1\ge3$$
columns beyond the nearer bar column.This is the required contradiction.The two row- $1$  inherited supports already suffice; the row- $4$  supports give the reflected argument using the bottom terminal. Both arguments exhibit two endpoint neighbours, so they also apply to the stronger completeness condition counting all retained occupied points.Thus every nonempty complete transverse-only pocket has  $n\ge2$ , and
$$\Phi(Y)\ge n\ge2.$$
Combining this with the exact chamber relation proves
$$\boxed{\Delta_{\rm chamber}\ge7.}$$
The empty pocket has exact increment  $5$ .5. The unequal-depth opposed pairs attain the bound with full local completenessLet  $N\ge10$  be even, and choose any even
$$4\le d,f\le N-6.$$
Take the right-facing source at bar  $0$ , with depths  $d,f$ , and the left-facing source at bar  $N-2$ , with depths
$$d'=N-2-d,\qquad f'=N-2-f.$$
These depths are even and at least four.Their bottom endpoint intervals are respectively
$$[0,d],\qquad[d+1,N-1],$$
and their top endpoint intervals are
$$[0,f],\qquad[f+1,N-1].$$
Thus both extreme rows are filled without overlap. In every interior row, their endpoints are exactly in columns
$$0,1,N-2,N-1.$$
The original endpoint sets are disjoint, and no original matching edge is changed or reassigned.Complete support accountingAt each seam, the two terminals consume one another’s beyond-tip supports. All new supports outside the pocket lie on its occupied horizontal boundary. All four inherited interior supports are consumed by the extreme bars.The entire remaining support set inside the pocket is
$$\begin{aligned}
H_1={}&
\{(1,c):c=3,5,\ldots,f-1\}\\
&{}\cup
\{(1,c):c=f+2,f+4,\ldots,N-4\},
\\[2mm]
H_4={}&
\{(4,c):c=3,5,\ldots,d-1\}\\
&{}\cup

The two support rows are three rows apart.Consequently no retained support has an adjacent retained support or an adjacent interior-row endpoint. Its sole occupied neighbour is its endpoint on row  $0$  or row  $5$ .This verifies local completeness for the full retained occupied set, rather than merely checking endpoint neighbours. $$F(Y)=\varnothing,\qquad E(Y)=\varnothing,\qquad
\boxed{\Phi(Y)=2}.$$
The whole-chamber increment is exactly
$$\boxed{5+2=7}.$$
This proves sharpness for every even  $W=N+2\ge12$ , including all the stated unequal-depth choices.Juxtaposed blocksFor consecutive blocks of even widths, every block starts at an even column. At an internal block boundary, the right bar of the earlier block and the left bar of the next are adjacent even-start bars facing away. Their interface crosses a tile-column boundary.Thus no cross-block mixed tile or event is introduced. The remaining supports stay separated from the neighbouring block’s endpoints, so local completeness persists. Each of the  $n=g+1$  inner originals has charge  $+1$ , creates four mixed tiles against the walls, and creates ten events. Its contribution against the common old-wall baseline is therefore

The contact regions of the inner originals are disjoint. Hence
$$\Phi(O)=1-n=-g.$$

$$6-g-k=5-k
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad g=1.$$
